A1.justification: Both PDFs describe P-SpikeSSM by the same authors. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original P-SpikeSSM benchmark accuracies, component ablations, timing measurements, and spiking-activity analyses in Section 4 and the figures.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a 35-class Speech Command result, a ReLU ablation, and sequential CIFAR-10 experiments.

M1.justification: The core neuronal dynamics, SpikeSampler surrogate, SpikeMixer, and ClampFuse architecture remain unchanged. v3 adds tested variants that replace GELU with ReLU and pass real-valued probabilities instead of sampled spikes, making limited changes to the evaluated procedures.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 extends speech evaluation from SC10 to the 35-class Speech Command task. Appendix D adds sequential CIFAR-10 experiments, but CIFAR-10 already underlies LRA Image in both versions; the PDFs do not sufficiently specify a distinct data representation to establish additional coverage beyond that retained dataset.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds numerical comparisons with PSN (88.45%) and Sliding PSN (86.70%), while noting their column-based inputs differ from P-SpikeSSM's pixel sequences. Section 4.1 also adds a qualitative speech-baseline comparison involving Bittar and Garner. Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 revises energy evaluation by counting convolution operations across all N neurons. New experiments introduce activation and spike-versus-probability controls. Existing accuracy metrics, stated splits, and training settings in Tables 4 and S1 remain unchanged; the added speech and CIFAR experiments provide limited further protocol detail.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds a GELU-to-ReLU ablation testing the accuracy cost of a hardware-friendly activation. Appendix D adds a spike-versus-real-valued-probability comparison on sequential CIFAR-10. The original surrogate, mixer, normalization, parameterization, neuron-count, and LIF comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v3 introduces no confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure. Accuracy tables retain point estimates, and the appendices add no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The central energy estimate changes substantially from over 70× to 36× following revised accounting in Section 4.2. Table 2 changes P-SpikeSSM's LRA Image accuracy from 80.60 to 82.40 under unchanged listed settings, reversing its ordering against BinaryS4D's retained 82.00. Newly reported results include 96.23% on 35-class speech, 80.40% for the ReLU ablation, and sequential CIFAR-10 accuracies of 85.6% with spikes and 87.2% with probabilities.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the analytical convolution-cost terms from L² to NL² for S4 and from IFRin·L² to IFRin·NL² for P-SpikeSSM, revising the resulting energy expressions. The main dynamical equations and convolution/HiPPO derivations in Appendices A–B remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the 'fully spiking' qualification from its benchmark claim, modestly revising the contribution's characterization. The abstract and conclusion otherwise retain the same claims about parallel probabilistic spiking, surrogate training, scalable architecture, strong SNN accuracy, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits energy estimates to arithmetic operations, excluding memory I/O, and clarifies GELU use in the comparison tables. It adds interpretations of the ReLU accuracy tradeoff and the loss of sparsity benefits when passing probabilities. Section 3.1.2 also removes the suggestion that spike sparsity enables Sparse FFT training.

D1.justification: The abstract adds an implementation repository link. Appendix D states that the new sequential CIFAR-10 experiment uses hyperparameters similar to LRA Image, providing limited configuration guidance. Existing hardware, discretization settings, memory figures, and Table S1 hyperparameters are retained; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for efficient alternatives to BPTT, plus references concerning parallel spiking neurons, speech recognition, quantized spiking language models, and hardware-friendly activation. It removes the Sparse FFT citation. The broader positioning against transformers, SSMs, and LIF-based approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording corrections and explanatory additions, updates the author affiliation, and adds acknowledgments and conference-publication headers. The principal section sequence and Appendices A–D remain intact, without extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 1b changes from a heatmap to a probability curve, and several figures are resized. Table 1 moves into the experimentation section, Table 4 moves alongside the hyperparameter discussion, Table 5 gains a row, and the comparison tables gain spiking-status annotations. The overall visual organization remains recognizable.

improvement.justification: v3 improves rigor by correcting the missing neuron factor in the energy analysis and explicitly limiting the resulting 36× estimate to arithmetic costs. The added activation and probability controls clarify practical tradeoffs, and the repository link improves reproducibility information. These are useful but bounded gains: new speech/CIFAR protocols remain briefly documented, and the PSN comparisons use different input representations.
